1. Market Overview & Transaction Summary

This analysis covers 5,000 Air Jordan resale transactions from January 2023 through September 2025. The average retail price across all transactions was $191.17, while the average resale price was $273.23, yielding an average profit margin of $82.06.

Of all transactions, 61.3% cleared above retail, confirming that while premium opportunities are common, a substantial share of transactions — particularly for Used-condition shoes — result in losses relative to MSRP. The mean resale-to-retail ratio of 1.43x indicates the typical transaction yields a modest markup, though the distribution is wide and bimodal.

2. Performance by Shoe Model & Colorway

Model-level analysis reveals significant variance in resale performance. Air Jordan 11 Retro leads on average profit margin at $99.84, while the lowest-performing model averages $50.52.

Colorway-level dispersion is even more pronounced. The Pine Green colorway commands the highest average margin at $89.23, driven by high collector demand and limited supply. Several colorways average below retail, indicating oversupply or weak demand relative to their model's retail price.

3. Impact of Shoe Condition on Resale Value

Condition is one of the strongest predictors of resale performance. Deadstock (Brand New) shoes achieve a 100.0% premium rate, while Used shoes only clear retail 0.0% of the time — a gap of 100.0% percentage points.

The average margin gap between Deadstock and VNDS is $226.38, and between VNDS and Used is $95.28. These gaps quantify the direct financial impact of condition degradation and should inform sourcing standards and pricing floors.

Sourcing Implication: The DS-to-VNDS margin gap of $226.38 suggests that sourcing Deadstock inventory commands a meaningful premium over VNDS — but the VNDS-to-Used gap of $95.28 is even larger, indicating that condition degradation below VNDS is disproportionately penalized by the market. Sourcing should prioritize Deadstock and VNDS; Used inventory requires acquisition at deep discounts to be viable.

4. Sales Channel Performance & Inventory Velocity

Channel performance is the core strategic tension in resale: the platform with the highest margins is not always the one that moves product fastest. Walk-in Retail leads on average profit margin at $89.55, while StockX has the fastest inventory turnover at 7.5 average days.

The interplay between margin and velocity is critical. A channel with high margins but slow turnover ties up capital; a fast-moving channel with thin margins generates volume but less per-unit profit. The bubble chart below visualizes this tradeoff directly.

6. Key Findings & Strategic Recommendations

Based on the analysis of 5,000 transactions, the following strategic recommendations equip resale analysts and sourcing strategists with actionable guidance.

Prioritize Deadstock Sourcing

Deadstock inventory commands a $264.01 average margin vs. $-57.66 for Used — a $321.67 spread. The premium rate for Deadstock is 100.0% vs. just 0.0% for Used. Sourcing standards should prioritize unworn inventory whenever possible; if acquiring Used stock, purchase only at deep discount to preserve margin.

Optimize Channel Selection

Walk-in Retail delivers the highest average margin at $89.55, while StockX moves inventory fastest at 7.5 days. For high-value Deadstock listings, favor the highest-margin channel to maximize per-unit profit. For VNDS or borderline inventory where turnover matters, prioritize velocity-oriented channels to free capital.

Target High-Margin Colorways

The Pine Green colorway leads all others at $89.23 average margin. Sourcing efforts should concentrate on the top 3–5 colorways identified in Section 2, while avoiding the below-retail segments documented in the combo table.

Time the Market

Seasonal analysis shows May yields the highest average margins ($95.22), while Oct is weakest ($60.36). Consider accumulating inventory during weaker months and listing during seasonal peaks to capture the spread.

Set a 30-Day Inventory Threshold

The overall average days in inventory is 22.5 days. Inventory held beyond 45 days erodes returns through carrying costs and price depreciation. Set a 30-day target for listing optimization and a 45-day hard review threshold to reprice or channel-shift stagnant stock.

Summary: The Air Jordan resale market rewards discipline — sourcing Deadstock in top colorways, listing on the right channel for the condition tier, and timing sales to seasonal demand peaks. The data shows that margin and velocity are inversely correlated across channels, so the optimal strategy is tiered: high-margin inventory on premium channels, fast-turn inventory on velocity channels. Avoid Used-condition inventory unless acquired at substantial discount, and steer clear of the below-retail model–colorway segments identified in this analysis.
